instruction: I want to use my work email account work-admin@company.com in Thunderbird, but I don't have access to the server settings (IMAP/POP3/SMTP server addresses and ports). Can you configure Thunderbird to automatically detect and set up this account without me providing any server configuration details?

metadata.explanation: This is an infeasible task variation. While Thunderbird does have autoconfiguration capabilities, it relies on either: (1) the email provider publishing configuration in their DNS records or at autoconfig.domain.com, or (2) Mozilla's ISPDB database of known providers. For a fictional/unknown company domain like 'company.com', neither of these would be available. Without the server discovering the configuration automatically AND without the user manually providing server details, the account setup cannot proceed beyond the initial screen, making this task infeasible.

llm_judge_reasons: Task is correctly marked as infeasible - Thunderbird cannot autoconfigure an email account for an unknown/fictional domain without server configuration details
The evaluator correctly uses the 'infeasible' function, which is the appropriate marker for tasks that cannot be completed due to environmental or logical impossibility
